title: Role Certification and Peer Shadow Rotation Handbook
author: Maya Chen
body:
Summary:
This handbook describes Redwood's Role Certification & Peer Shadow Rotation Program (RCSR). The program standardizes how contributors validate role readiness, run structured shadow rotations, and earn role-level certifications (badges) that feed into promotion and mobility decisions. It is intended for ICs, managers, people-ops partners, and mentors across all functions.

Goals:
- Reduce ambiguity in role expectations and promotion signals.
- Provide repeatable, job-relevant learning through structured on-the-job shadowing.
- Create lightweight, auditable artifacts for promotion committees and career conversations.

Scope:
- Applies to all IC and manager role families at Redwood (Engineering, Product, SRE, Customer Success, Sales, People Ops).
- Supports lateral rotations and short-term shadow stints (2–12 weeks), and role certification tracks for career progression.
- Integrates with existing onboarding tooling (training playbooks, badge registry, and the internal LMS).

Key Definitions:
- Role Certification: A documented assessment confirming the contributor meets the role's competency checklist and can work independently at the target level.
- Peer Shadow Rotation: A time-boxed period where a candidate works alongside a role-holder to observe, practice, and own low-risk tasks under mentorship.
- Certification Panel: A small group (2–3) reviewers who confirm evidence for certification.

Program Components:
1) Competency Checklists (per role/level)
   - Each checklist is owned by the role lead and published in Confluence (competencies framed as observable behaviors).
   - Example items: "Delivers production change independently with < 1 rollback per quarter", "Authors ROI-driven feature proposals that include performance/cost estimates".

2) Shadow Rotation Workflow (recommended cadence)
   - Pre-rotation (Week 0): Candidate and manager submit an intake form in the onboarding tool with goals, scope, and required systems access.
   - Orientation (Day 1): 2-hour onboarding with mentor covering team context, key systems, escalation paths.
   - Observational Phase (Week 1): Candidate joins standups, reads runbooks, and shadows 3–5 core tasks.
   - Gradual Ownership (Weeks 2–4+): Candidate performs low-risk tasks, pair-programs, and operates under mentor-approved checklist items.
   - Reflection & Evidence (Final week): Candidate compiles artifacts (PRs, incident postmortems, design notes) and a short reflection document.

3) Certification Assessment
   - Submission: Candidate links artifacts to the certification form and requests a panel review.
   - Panel composition: 1 role lead, 1 peer reviewer from outside the candidate's immediate team, 1 people-ops representative (optional for non-manager certifications).
   - Assessment criteria: completeness of artifacts, alignment to competency checklist, demonstrated impact, and ability to describe tradeoffs.
   - Decision outcomes: certified | request-more-evidence | declined. Panel adds a 2–3 sentence rationale to the record.

4) Badge Issuance & Recordkeeping
   - Successful certifications create a badge entry in the internal LMS and a Confluence record under /company-handbook/02_roles-and-career/badges (automated via the onboarding tool).
   - Records include date, reviewers, artifacts, and candidate reflection.

5) Integration with Promotions & Mobility
   - Certification is one form of evidence considered by promotion panels. It is not an automatic promotion trigger but substantially de-risks decisions.
   - Lateral moves that rely on certification may have reduced ramp expectations.

Roles & Responsibilities:
- Candidate: completes artifacts, actively participates in shadowing, and communicates blockers.
- Manager (origin team): approves time allocation and supports access requests.
- Mentor (host role-holder): designs the rotation plan, provides feedback, and signs off on competency items.
- Role Lead: maintains competency checklist and serves on panels as needed.
- People Ops: runs program guidelines, schedules panels on request, records badge metadata.

Operational Rules & Constraints:
- Rotations must not exceed 20% of candidate's weekly capacity unless manager-approved and budgeted.
- Shadow rotations that cross customer-facing oncall or sales quotas require explicit risk sign-off from the hosting manager.
- Two concurrent active certifications for the same candidate are discouraged.

Templates & Examples:
1) Rotation Intake form (fields)
   - Candidate name | Current role & level | Target role/level | Duration | Primary mentor | Goals (3 bullets) | Systems to access | Training prerequisites
2) Artifact checklist (sample for Senior Engineer certification)
   - 1–2 merged PRs with peer review comments showing system-level reasoning
   - One performance or cost optimization with measurable impact estimate
   - A short design note (<= 1500 words) describing a tradeoff the candidate led
   - Evidence of cross-team communication (meeting notes, RFC comments)

Table: Typical Rotation Durations by Purpose
| Purpose | Recommended length | Typical outcome |
| Shadow exploration (low risk) | 2 weeks | Candidate learns the role surface area |
| Skill transfer (feature ownership) | 4–8 weeks | Candidate executes and owns 1–2 tasks |
| Accreditation (certification-ready) | 6–12 weeks | Candidate accumulates evidence for panel review |

Sample Panel Rubric (scoring 1–4 each)
- Technical/role aptitude (1–4)
- Independent delivery (1–4)
- Communication & cross-team collaboration (1–4)
- Impact orientation & cost-awareness (1–4)
Total >= 12 recommended to certify; panels weigh narrative comments more than raw score.

Automation & Tools:
- Onboarding tool: create rotation intake, auto-generate access tickets, and calendar blocks for orientation sessions.
- Badge registry: internal LMS endpoint /api/v1/badges (POST) to create records. Example payload (internal use):
{
  "candidate":"alice@example.com",
  "badge":"senior-engineer-cert-2026",
  "date":"2026-09-15",
  "artifacts":["PR-123","DOC-456"]
}
(Teams should not hard-code API keys; use the onboarding tool connector.)

Privacy & Sensitivity:
- Artifacts that include customer data must be redacted or submitted through the secure evidence channel.
- Certification records are internal; sensitive narrative comments marked for people-ops review only should be flagged as restricted.

Common Playbook: How to Run a 6-Week Certification Rotation (step-by-step)
1) Week -1: Candidate discusses goals with manager and nominates a mentor. People Ops creates a rotation record.
2) Week 0: Mentor drafts a 6-week plan with measurable milestones and shares it in Confluence.
3) Week 1–2: Observation + small tasks; candidate completes 1–2 low-risk tickets.
4) Week 3–4: Candidate leads a small feature or process improvement; mentor moves to consult mode.
5) Week 5: Candidate compiles artifacts and writes reflection; mentor provides final feedback.
6) Week 6: Panel review and decision within 5 business days. People Ops publishes the outcome.

Escalation & Dispute Resolution:
- If a candidate or manager disputes a panel decision, they may request a re-review within 14 days. Re-review includes an additional role lead not on the original panel.
- People Ops mediates conflicts and may recommend a remediation plan (additional shadow weeks, targeted training).

Measuring Success (KPIs):
- Time-to-certification (median weeks)
- Percentage of certified candidates who retain in-role for 12 months
- Manager satisfaction (quarterly survey)
- Diversity of certified candidates by function and region

Frequently Asked Questions (abridged):
Q: Does certification replace performance reviews?
A: No. Certification is complementary evidence used in promotion and mobility decisions but does not replace the normal review cycle.

Q: Can external hires use the program to accelerate compensation leveling?
A: Yes — hiring managers may nominate strong lateral hires for a shortened certification track (typically 4 weeks) with a focused artifact checklist.
